# Reminder tone and structure

Write in the company's voice (`brand.voice`). Reminders are sent by a person, under their name.

## Tone by customer score

| Score | Tone | Opening example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Good payer | Friendly, assumes an oversight | "A quick note in case this slipped through..." |
| Occasionally late | Clear and polite, states the date | "Invoice 1043 for USD 1,200 was due on 03/15/2026 and is still open." |
| Repeat late | Firm, factual, asks for a date | "We have not yet received payment for invoices 1043 and 1051, now 47 days overdue. Please confirm when we can expect payment." |

## Every reminder includes

- Invoice numbers, amounts with currency code and due dates.
- How to pay, using the details the user provides (never invent bank details or links).
- A clear ask: pay, or reply with a date or a question.
- A contact for disputes.

## Never

- Threats, legal language, mentions of credit reporting or collection agencies (those decisions belong to a person and may be regulated).
- Late fees or interest the user's terms do not state.
- Shaming language or messages to anyone other than the billing contact.

## Subject line patterns

- "Invoice 1043: payment reminder"
- "Overdue invoices 1043 and 1051, please confirm a payment date"
